chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Nadr ibn Shu'ayb, from Abd al-Ghaffar al-Jazi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who left Mina intending to go to the House (Kaaba) before the middle of the night, and thus spent the morning in Mecca. He said: 'It is not valid for him until he gives charity or sheds blood. But if he left Mina after the middle of the night, nothing harms him.'

key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a sacred site near Mecca where pilgrims spend days of Hajj
key_terms.نِصْفِ اللَّيْلِ: The middle of the night (specifically referring to the time before Fajr prayer)
key_terms.يُهْرِقَ دَمًا: Sheds blood (referring to the sacrifice of an animal, i.e., Hady)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for leaving Mina before Fajr during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the temporal boundary for the 'Qada al-Hajj' ritual of leaving Mina, distinguishing between pre-dawn and post-dawn departures. In Shia jurisprudence, leaving before the middle of the night necessitates a compensatory act (such as charity or animal sacrifice) to rectify the haste, whereas leaving after this time is considered valid without penalty. This ruling underscores the importance of adhering to the prescribed timing of Hajj rituals to ensure the completeness of the pilgrimage.
